title: legacy mlruns detection: check only <experiment>/meta.yaml per numeric dir via os.scandir, never walk experiment contents
answers: Why does MLflow startup take a long time or slow down when a local mlruns folder has many experiments and artifacts and no tracking URI is set?
Where is the check that detects existing legacy file-store mlruns data when no tracking URI is configured?
Why does MLflow treat a non-numeric folder or a folder without meta.yaml as not legacy data?
How does the backward-compatibility fallback decide between the SQLite default and the old ./mlruns file store?
body:
Path: Tracking URI resolution with no URI configured calls mlflow/tracking/_tracking_service/utils.py:_has_existing_mlruns_data to decide whether a local ./mlruns directory holds legacy file-store experiments; it runs on every default-tracking lookup, so cost matters.
Rule: Discovery lists only the top level of DEFAULT_LOCAL_FILE_AND_ARTIFACT_PATH with os.scandir, keeps entries that are directories with a purely numeric name, and checks os.path.join(entry.path, FileStore.META_DATA_FILE_NAME) with os.path.lexists. It must not iterdir() or enumerate experiment contents, because that made the check scale with the number of artifact files (about 13x slower on 20 experiments x 20 files in the PR's benchmark).
Rule: Use lexists rather than exists or is_file so that any entry named meta.yaml counts (including directories and symlinks), preserving the prior behavior.
Rule: Any OSError from scandir (missing mlruns, permissions) returns False; a missing mlruns directory is covered by this rather than a separate exists() pre-check.
Constraints: Applies only to the legacy-data probe. Non-numeric directories are ignored and a meta.yaml at mlruns top level is not considered. Does not validate the contents of meta.yaml. FileStore is deprecated, so the probe only decides the fallback path.
applies: Local default tracking-URI resolution in mlflow/tracking/_tracking_service; not for the FileStore read/write code itself.
says: MLflow startup is slow when a local mlruns folder has many experiments and artifacts and no tracking URI is set
Default tracking URI lookup slows down with many artifact files in the local mlruns folder
MLflow treats a folder without meta.yaml as legacy file store data when no tracking URI is configured
Non-numeric folders in mlruns are ignored when detecting old file store experiments
Fallback between the SQLite default and the old mlruns file store picks the wrong backend
search: Legacy mlruns detection used for default tracking URI resolution: it scans only the top level of the local mlruns directory with a non-recursive scan, keeping numeric-named directories that contain a meta.yaml entry (lexists, so directories and symlinks count). It never walks experiment contents, and any OS error returns false. Only decides the fallback path; FileStore is deprecated.
